edges.description: Biallelic loss-of-function FH variants abolish or severely reduce fumarase enzyme activity.
Loss of fumarase activity blocks the fumarate-to-malate step of the Krebs cycle.
Blocking the hydration step causes the upstream substrate fumarate to accumulate.
Accumulated fumarate is excreted, producing elevated urinary fumaric acid.
Accumulated fumarate succinates cysteine residues of iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis proteins.
Fumarate is the product of the succinate dehydrogenase (complex II) reaction, so its accumulation product-inhibits complex II.
Defective iron-sulfur cluster assembly impairs the function of complex I, which depends on these clusters.
Complex II suppression contributes to combined respiratory chain dysfunction and decreased respiration.
Complex I deficiency reduces electron transport and mitochondrial respiration.
Reduced oxidative ATP production impairs energy supply to the high-demand developing brain.
intermediate_mechanisms: Reduced oxidative ATP output limits energy available to energy-demanding neural tissue.

edges.description: Reduced oxidative ATP production produces a generalized energy deficit affecting growth and feeding.
intermediate_mechanisms: Systemic impairment of oxidative energy metabolism.

edges.description: Brain energy failure produces a severe neonatal and infantile encephalopathy.
Cerebral metabolic dysfunction causes seizures.
Cerebral energy failure contributes to hypotonia.
Impaired brain energy metabolism causes severe, global developmental delay.
A fetal and early-life energy deficit disturbs cortical brain development.
intermediate_mechanisms: In utero energy-metabolism failure perturbs neuronal proliferation and cortical organization.

edges.description: Disordered cortical development manifests as diffuse polymicrogyria.
Brain imaging shows cerebral atrophy.
Brain imaging shows enlarged ventricles.
Brain imaging shows an abnormal (thin or absent) corpus callosum.
Brain imaging shows delayed myelination for age.
Many affected individuals are microcephalic.
Brain imaging shows an abnormally small brain stem.
Poor weight gain and growth deficiency manifest as failure to thrive.
Poor feeding is an early manifestation.
Lethargy is an early manifestation of the energy deficit.
FH-deficient cell lines reproduce decreased respiration and combined respiratory chain dysfunction downstream of fumarate accumulation.
edges.limitations: The models are cancer-derived and mouse cell lines studied in the context of FH-deficient tumorigenesis rather than the neuronal tissue affected in the recessive neurometabolic disease, so translational fidelity to the developing human brain is uncertain.
edges.source: FH-deficient human and mouse cell lines

nodes.description: Missense variant (p.Ala308Thr) at the fumarase intersubunit interface, associated with fumarate hydratase deficiency. Biochemical characterization showed severely diminished activity due to defective oligomerization, with the enzyme forming homodimers rather than homotetramers.

evidence.snippet: We conclude that A308T and H318Y render human fumarase enzymatically inactive via defective oligomerization.
